original_question: Does there exist a planar graph G whose list packing number chi*_l(G) is at least 6?
target_in_paper: Section 2, subsection "Planar graphs", Problem 2.6: the open problem asking whether there exists a planar graph G with χ^*_ℓ(G) ≥ 6.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct graph class (planar graphs), the correct invariant (the list packing number χ^*_ℓ(G)), and the correct threshold (at least 6). It is essentially the same open problem as the paper’s Problem 2.6.
missing_details: The draft does not define χ^*_ℓ(G). In the paper, χ^*_ℓ(G) is the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits an L-packing of size k.
The draft does not define a k-list-assignment: a list-assignment L assigns to each vertex v a set L(v) of available colors, and it is a k-list-assignment when |L(v)| = k for every vertex v.
The draft does not define an L-coloring: a coloring φ with φ(v) ∈ L(v) for every vertex v.
The draft does not define when an L-coloring is proper: adjacent vertices must receive distinct colors.
The draft does not define what it means for L-colorings to be disjoint: for every vertex v and distinct indices i,j, one has φ_i(v) ≠ φ_j(v).
To be fully stand-alone, the existential quantifier should be explicit: the question asks whether there exists at least one planar graph G with this property.
The paper’s formulation imposes no extra restrictions such as bipartite, cubic, outerplanar, triangle-free, or prescribed girth; those would broaden or alter the target problem.

No algebraic ambient structure, degree condition, homogeneity condition, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic qualifier is involved here; the hidden content is entirely in the graph-theoretic and list-packing definitions.
refined_question: Does there exist a planar graph G such that χ^*_ℓ(G) ≥ 6, where χ^*_ℓ(G) is the least integer k with the property that for every list-assignment L satisfying |L(v)| = k for all v ∈ V(G), there exist k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings φ_1, …, φ_k of G; that is, φ_i(v) ∈ L(v) for every v, each φ_i is proper, and φ_i(v) ≠ φ_j(v) for every vertex v and all distinct i,j?
justification: The cited paper is a workshop open-problems note, so the nearest official target is an open problem rather than a theorem or conjecture. In Section 2, after introducing list-assignments, proper L-colorings, disjointness, L-packings, and the definition of χ^*_ℓ(G), the subsection "Planar graphs" states exactly Problem 2.6, which is your draft question. The only substantive issue with the draft is that it is not fully stand-alone unless the paper’s earlier definitions of list packing are imported.
